n:AXIS Capital Holdings Limited: AXIS Capital Holdings Limited is a company based in Pembroke, Bermuda. Its tie to a central bank runs through one person. Cheryl-Ann Lister was Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Bermuda Monetary Authority from 1999 to 2006. On 23 September 2008 AXIS announced that she had joined its board as an independent director, meaning a board member who is not an employee of the company.
n:Accountant General, Government of Beli: The Accountant General, in Belmopan, prepares the financial statements of the Government of Belize. For the 2011/2012 financial year the Auditor General of Belize reported that the Treasury could not show that 25 accounts held at the Central Bank of Belize for the government had been reconciled, that is checked and matched, for the period audited. The same report found that public debt records kept by the central bank did not agree with the Accountant General's statements, and that interest payments it recorded differed from the government's own system.
n:American Bank of Albania: The American Bank of Albania is a bank in Tirana. Gent Sejko, who became Governor of the Bank of Albania and chairman of its Supervisory Council on 5 February 2015, had held senior executive and committee-chairing posts at the American Bank of Albania earlier in his career, along with similar roles at the National Commercial Bank and Raiffeisen Bank. He moved into the governorship from Deputy General Manager of Societe Generale Albania.
n:Arab African International Bank: The Arab African International Bank is a bank in Cairo. Its link to Egypt's central bank is a career move by one of its own executives. Hassan Abdalla was vice chairman and managing director of the Arab African International Bank, and he left that job to become Governor of the Central Bank of Egypt on 18 August 2022, the post he has held since.
n:Arab Petroleum Investments Corporation: The Arab Petroleum Investments Corporation, or APICORP, is an agency based in Dammam, Saudi Arabia. Rasheed Mohammed Al Maraj was its General Manager and Chief Executive Officer, and before that Assistant Under-Secretary at the Ministry of Finance and National Economy and Under-Secretary at the Ministry of Transportation. He left APICORP to become Governor of the Central Bank of Bahrain, a post he has held since January 2005.
n:Arion Bank: Arion Bank is a bank in Reykjavik, the later name of Kaupthing Bank. Asgeir Jonsson was chief economist there and head of its research department. He left that work to become Governor of the Central Bank of Iceland, on a five-year term that began on 20 August 2019. The move was from research in a commercial bank to running the country's central bank.
n:Asian Development Bank: The Asian Development Bank is an international lender based in Manila. Enkhjargal Danzanbaljir was Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mongolia from 2007 to 2010 and its representative in London, then went out to work at the Asian Development Bank, among other institutions including the World Bank and the state-owned State Bank of Mongolia, and returned to the Bank of Mongolia as a member of its Supervisory Board in 2025.
n:Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, or AIIB, is an international lender based in Beijing. Enkhjargal Danzanbaljir was Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mongolia from 2007 to 2010 and its representative in London, then worked outside it at the AIIB and at other institutions including the World Bank and the state-owned State Bank of Mongolia, before returning to the Bank of Mongolia as a member of its Supervisory Board in 2025.
n:Baker Tilly Moldova: Baker Tilly Moldova is a company in Moldova. Constantin Schendra was its executive director from 2015 to 2018, work he took up after spells as a senior auditor at Ernst & Young. He then crossed into the National Bank of Moldova, running its Banking Supervision Department from 2018 to 2021, and on 4 November 2021 became Deputy Governor and a member of the bank's Executive Committee.
n:Banco AV Villas: Banco AV Villas is a bank in Bogota. Gerardo Hernandez Correa had been a codirector of the Banco de la Republica, Colombia's central bank, as well as its executive manager and the secretary of its Board. He left for the commercial side, becoming vice-president of legal affairs at Banco de Bogota from 2021, and was then named president of Banco AV Villas in an announcement on 27 June 2024.
n:Banco Angolano de Investimentos (BAI): Banco Angolano de Investimentos, or BAI, is a bank in Luanda. Jose de Lima Massano was its chief executive, and an executive director of the state-owned BPC, before becoming Governor of the Banco Nacional de Angola, Angola's central bank, which he led for close to ten years between 2010 and 2023. He was also elected to BAI's board on 18 August 2015, taking office that 1 September. In June 2023 he left the central bank to become Senior Minister in the President's office.
n:Banco Basa: Banco Basa is a bank in Paraguay. Carlos Fernandez Valdovinos was President of the Banco Central del Paraguay, the country's central bank, from 2013 to 2018. After leaving that post he joined Banco Basa as a member of its board of directors, moving from the head of the institution that oversees the country's money to the board of a commercial bank.
n:Banco de Bogotá: Banco de Bogota is a bank in Bogota. Gerardo Hernandez Correa had served as a codirector of the Banco de la Republica, Colombia's central bank, and also as its executive manager and the secretary of its Board. From 2021 he worked at Banco de Bogota as vice-president of legal affairs. He was later named president of Banco AV Villas, announced on 27 June 2024.
n:Banco de Poupança e Crédito (BPC): Banco de Poupanca e Credito, or BPC, is a state-owned bank in Luanda. Jose de Lima Massano was an executive director there, and chief executive of Banco BAI, before becoming Governor of the Banco Nacional de Angola, Angola's central bank, a job he held for close to ten years between 2010 and 2023. He left the central bank in June 2023 to become Senior Minister in the President's office.
n:Banka Kombëtare Tregtare: Banka Kombetare Tregtare is a bank in Tirana. Its link to the Bank of Albania is one man's career. Gent Sejko held senior executive posts and chaired committees at Banka Kombetare Tregtare and at other Albanian banks, and came from Deputy General Manager of Societe Generale Albania to become Governor of the Bank of Albania and chairman of its Supervisory Council on 5 February 2015.
n:Belize Electricity Limited: Belize Electricity Limited is a company in Belize. Kareem Michael joined the Central Bank of Belize as a monetary economist in 2000 and was Deputy Director of its Research Department from 2008. In 2014 he left to be a senior business analyst at Belize Electricity Limited, then returned to the central bank as Deputy Governor in November 2017, Acting Governor on 13 August 2021 and Governor on 1 December 2021.
n:Bolsa Electrónica de Valores del Urugu: The Bolsa Electronica de Valores del Uruguay, or BEVSA, is an electronic securities exchange in Montevideo. Diego Labat was President of the Banco Central del Uruguay, the country's central bank, from 2020 to 2024. The year after that term ended, BEVSA's board named him its General Manager, a decision taken on 20 August 2025.
n:CBZ Holdings Limited: CBZ Holdings Limited is a commercial banking group based in Harare. John Mangudya was its chief executive, and he left that job to run Zimbabwe's central bank, taking over as Governor of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe from 1 May 2014. That step from the top of a commercial bank into the governorship is the tie between the two.
n:Demerara Bank Limited: Demerara Bank Limited is a bank in Georgetown, Guyana. Rajendra Rampersaud sat as a Director at the Bank of Guyana, the country's central bank, until 2018. After that he became a Director of Demerara Bank Limited, moving from the board of the central bank to the board of a commercial bank.
n:Directorate of Public Prosecutions of: The Directorate of Public Prosecutions, in Gaborone, brings criminal cases on behalf of the state in Botswana. Headed by Stephen Tiroyakgosi, it called in Moses Pelaelo, Governor of the Bank of Botswana, to hear his account of 100 billion pula that the state alleged had been looted from the central bank by former president Ian Khama and former intelligence chief Isaac Kgosi. Those allegations are unproven. Tiroyakgosi said Pelaelo told them no money is missing from the Bank of Botswana, and that the investigation was continuing.
n:Ecobank Transnational Incorporated: Ecobank Transnational Incorporated is a bank with its base in Lome, Togo. Sheila M'mbijjewe was a non-executive director of Ecobank, meaning a board member who does not work in the business day to day, as well as a director of Standard Chartered Bank and a board member of PricewaterhouseCoopers. She left that set of roles to become Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Kenya.
n:Ernst & Young Cyprus: Ernst & Young Cyprus is an accounting and audit firm in Cyprus. Constantin Schendra worked there as a senior auditor from 2013 to 2014, part of a career in auditing that also took in Ernst & Young Moldova and an executive director post at Baker Tilly Moldova. He then joined the National Bank of Moldova, heading its Banking Supervision Department from 2018 to 2021 and becoming Deputy Governor on 4 November 2021.
n:Ernst & Young Moldova: Ernst & Young Moldova is an accounting and audit firm in Chisinau. Constantin Schendra was a senior auditor there from 2010 to 2015, and worked in auditing elsewhere afterwards. He then moved into the National Bank of Moldova, where he ran the Banking Supervision Department from 2018 to 2021 before being made Deputy Governor and a member of the Executive Committee on 4 November 2021.
n:Farallon Capital Management LLC: Farallon Capital Management LLC is a company based in the United States. Greg Swart was its Managing Member and Chief Financial Officer from 2002 to 2019, and had spent about twelve years at Goldman Sachs before that. He then took a seat as a Director on the board of the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority, moving from private finance to the body that oversees it.
n:Financial Intelligence Agency of Botsw: The Financial Intelligence Agency is based in Gaborone. Botswana's Directorate on Corruption and Economic Crime confirmed it was investigating unaccounted-for funds on government accounts held at the Bank of Botswana, after the Auditor General reported that 22 billion pula in receipts and payments remained unaccounted for. The Financial Intelligence Agency was reported to have opened its own investigation into the same accounts, which its Director General would neither confirm nor deny. The investigations are open and nothing is proven.
